source.title: Calendar feature geometry in GPT-2 layer 8 residual stream SAEs

record.tranche_reason: The post compares feature activation patterns and decoder-space geometry across GPT-2 SAE dictionary sizes. This bears on feature splitting, but it does not use the original study's method.
record.gate_note: The post reports explicit splitting and geometry observations for weekdays and months, and a more complex result for calendar years. It cites other work's weekday result, but the rows below describe this post's own analysis. No separate outcomes are reported in text for every SAE size; figure details that are not described in the text are not inferred.
record.test_reason: The post compares weekday, month and calendar-year features across GPT-2 layer 8 residual SAEs of 768 to 98304 latents. It reports coarse features splitting into finer ones and their decoder geometry, using its own PCA-based method rather than the original's.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The authors report weekday and month splitting across SAE sizes, a more complex year pattern, and a temporal direction ordering year and non-year features. They call the ordering imperfect and the clustering method exploratory.
record.recipe_differences: The post selects features from activation patterns and examines their decoder directions with PCA, UMAP, and clustering, rather than reproducing the original method. It studies GPT-2 layer 8 residual-stream SAEs.
record.method_sensitivity: The calendar-year PCA pattern depends on including multi-year features; the post says PCA on single-year features only succeeds for a few 21st-century features and does not explain the 20th-century features.

fits_no_version.finding: A temporal direction in the PCA of calendar-year decoder directions orders non-year features (e.g. Hussein, Obama, Trump) by historical period. It matches no SAE feature and no global PCA component.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE decoder space contains interpretable linear structure (e.g. a timeline direction) across features, not captured by single latents.

fits_no_version.finding: HDBSCAN on a UMAP of decoder directions recovers a single-year feature cluster but not weekday or month clusters. Most clusters are uninterpretable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unsupervised clustering of decoder directions can recover some feature families.

record.problems: The post gives no quantitative uncertainty or controls. Some interpretations are explicitly described as imperfect, and the calendar-year non-year feature labels are a manually selected random subsample for which the authors could assign a relevant period. The clustering approach did not recover weekday or month clusters, and most feature clusters were not interpretable.
record.rows_left_out: No separate row for every SAE size: the text explicitly describes the smallest and largest weekday SAEs and gives broader size-range statements for months and years, but does not state results for intermediate sizes individually. Figure-only details not described in the text were not extracted.

untested.parts: Whether the finer features jointly cover the coarse feature's inputs. Direction similarity is not quantified beyond PCA plots.
Large models and standard open SAE releases. Only GPT-2 small layer 8 SAEs are studied, from the stitching-SAEs post.
Nested hierarchical families mirroring a concept hierarchy.
Absorption or parent latents failing to fire.
Decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, novel latents, and atomicity.
Causal role of the sparsity objective, and alternatives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post with no quantitative measures, controls or uncertainty. Evidence is qualitative descriptions of PCA figures. The 12-layer GPT-2 setting goes slightly beyond a one-layer model, but it is not a large model or standard open release, so V2 is left untested.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not establish that the smaller feature's inputs are completely partitioned among the larger features, or quantify how much of the coarse feature's input set they cover.
The analysis is of GPT-2 layer 8 SAEs; it does not test whether the pattern generalizes across large models or open SAE releases.
The post does not test whether split features form nested families that mirror a hierarchy of concepts.
It does not test absorption, parent-child firing gaps, or whether changing SAE size or sparsity fixes them.
It does not compare decompositions of larger and smaller SAE latents or test whether dictionaries contain a complete atomic set.
It does not test whether the splitting is caused by the SAE objective or compare objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

Months: the smallest SAE's single feature splits into many specific features; no counts are given. Sole author: Patrick Leask. The pack header flags 1 shared author name with an original but does not say which original.
statements.problem: The text says the smallest SAE's weekday feature lies near the mean of all the weekday features, not just the single-day ones. Also, the 'why' says pack headers do not link this study to an original, but this pack's header says it shares 1 author name with an original.

statements.correction: Weekdays and months: the smallest SAE's single feature splits into many specific features. Years: a more complex pattern. Most features cover year ranges or decade starts and ends, and more than a few single-year features appear only in the largest SAEs.
statements.problem: The text does not say calendar years mostly do not split. It calls the year case 'more complex', and finer single-year features do appear in the largest SAEs.
